There are 168089 such integers. I counted the complement, the numbers that are not divisible by any cube greater than 1.

A number is divisible by some perfect cube greater than 1 exactly when it is divisible by p³ for some prime p. So the numbers I want are those that are not cube-free.

With N = 999999, the number of cube-free integers in [1, N] is

Σ μ(k)·⌊N/k³⌋, for k = 1, …, 99,

since 100³ = 10⁶ exceeds N.

I computed each term for the squarefree k up to 99; all other k have μ(k) = 0.

- The positive terms (k = 1 and those k with μ(k) = +1) sum to 1,006,707.
- The negative terms (those k with μ(k) = −1) sum to 174,797.

The cube-free count is therefore 1,006,707 − 174,797 = 831,910. As a sanity check, 831,910/999,999 ≈ 0.8319, which matches 1/ζ(3) ≈ 0.8319.

The count of numbers divisible by some cube greater than 1 is 999,999 − 831,910 = 168,089.

ANSWER: 168089
